title: What If Lightning Struck the Open Ocean? Most Fish Survive

scenes.text: What if lightning hit the open sea? You'd expect every fish nearby to die. Most don't.
A single bolt can carry around 300 million volts and 30,000 amps.
But the current spreads out across the surface instead of plunging down.
Salt water conducts so well that the energy disperses sideways, fast.
Fish within a few meters of the surface can be hurt or killed. Deeper fish are mostly unaffected.
Swimmers are the ones at risk. A safe distance from a strike is about 30 meters, and about 90 percent of lightning hits land anyway.
